properties.name: local.server.port
properties.description: The port the server listens on, set once it listens (also in `WebServerInitializedEvent`). Nothing reads it from configuration: it is put there for the application to read.

properties.name: server.address
properties.description: The address to listen on. `localhost` is `127.0.0.1`; a host name is looked up. Default: all interfaces; **127.0.0.1 in Flutter apps**.

properties.name: server.compression.enabled
properties.description: Gzip of the responses of `mime-types`, from `min-response-size` on (or of unknown length), for clients that send `Accept-Encoding: gzip`; never partial content, nor an answer with a strong `ETag` (as Tomcat).

properties.name: server.compression.mime-types
properties.description: The media types compressed, as in Spring Boot; add `text/event-stream` to compress event streams.

properties.name: server.compression.min-response-size
properties.description: The smallest `Content-Length` compressed.

properties.name: server.connection-timeout
properties.description: How long a request body may send nothing while it is read: then the answer is 408 and the connection closes. `-1`, `0` or less: no timeout. Also how long an idle connection stays open.

properties.name: server.context-path
properties.description: A prefix of every mapping, such as `/shop`.

properties.name: server.forward-headers-strategy
properties.description: Behind a reverse proxy: apply its `Forwarded` or `X-Forwarded-Proto`, `-Host`, `-Port`, `-For` headers (the scheme, so cookies get `Secure` behind TLS; the host and port; the client's address), from trusted proxies only.

properties.name: server.forward-headers.trusted-proxies
properties.description: Whose forwarded headers are believed (Tomcat's `internalProxies`): IP addresses and CIDR ranges, as a comma list or a YAML list. A client reaching the server from elsewhere cannot set them. Default: loopback and private networks.

properties.name: server.isolates.cooldown
properties.description: The pause after a scaling step before the policy takes another.

properties.name: server.isolates.count
properties.description: How many isolates serve at the start: a number, or `auto` for one per processor core. `1` (the default): the application's own isolate only.

properties.name: server.isolates.drain-timeout
properties.description: How long an isolate that leaves the pool may finish its requests before it is stopped anyway.

properties.name: server.isolates.max
properties.description: The most isolates scaling goes up to; not set: the processor cores, or [count] when that is more.

properties.name: server.isolates.min
properties.description: The fewest isolates scaling goes down to.

properties.name: server.isolates.scale-down-after
properties.description: How long the isolates must be free before the policy removes one.

properties.name: server.isolates.scale-up-after
properties.description: How long the isolates must be late (see [scaleUpLag]) before the policy adds some.

properties.name: server.isolates.scale-up-lag
properties.description: How late the isolates' event loops run on average when the policy calls them overloaded: requests wait about that long before they are even looked at.

properties.name: server.isolates.scaling
properties.description: Who changes the number of isolates while the server runs: `manual` (the default: only the application, through the `IsolateScaler` bean) or `auto` (the scaling policy too, between [min] and [max]).

properties.name: server.max-concurrent-requests
properties.description: The most requests one isolate answers at a time (event streams not counted); a request past it is answered 503 with `Retry-After` at once, instead of waiting behind the others; its connection stays open for the next try. Not set: no limit.

properties.name: server.max-connections
properties.description: The most connections one isolate keeps open. While it has more, every request is answered 503 and its connection closed, until the number is back under the limit (counted at most every 100 ms). Not set: no limit. With a pool of isolates (`server.isolates.*`) each isolate has this many.

properties.name: server.max-http-request-body-size
properties.description: A larger request body is answered with 413, whatever its `Content-Type`; `-1` means no limit.

properties.name: server.mime-mappings.*
properties.description: More media types of the static resources by file extension, on top of the built-in ones (`server.mime-mappings.wasm=application/wasm`); an extension listed here wins. The extension is matched in any case.

properties.name: server.port
properties.description: The port. `0` picks a free one; the real port is then in `local.server.port`.

properties.name: server.request-timeout
properties.description: The longest a request's filters and handler may take to answer, else a 503; also a deadline for the calls the request makes. Default: no limit (`0` or less: none). Not in Spring Boot.

properties.name: server.retry-after
properties.description: The `Retry-After` of a 503 for a server that is full ([maxConnections], [maxConcurrentRequests]).

properties.name: server.session.cookie.domain
properties.description: The domain of the session cookie. Default: none, so the cookie goes back only to the host that set it.

properties.name: server.session.cookie.http-only
properties.description: Whether the session cookie is hidden from scripts.

properties.name: server.session.cookie.name
properties.description: The name of the session cookie.

properties.name: server.session.cookie.path
properties.description: The path of the session cookie. Default: the context path, or `/`.

properties.name: server.session.cookie.same-site
properties.description: The `SameSite` attribute of the session cookie; `unset` sends none.

properties.name: server.session.cookie.secure
properties.description: Whether the session cookie is sent over HTTPS only. Default: not set: it is secure when the request was.

properties.name: server.session.max-sessions
properties.description: The most sessions kept at once; `-1` for no limit.

properties.name: server.session.timeout
properties.description: How long a session lives without a request; a number without a unit is seconds.

properties.name: server.shutdown
properties.description: What happens to running requests when the server stops: `graceful` accepts no new connections and lets them finish, `immediate` cuts them.

properties.name: server.ssl.certificate
properties.description: The certificate chain (a PEM file); TLS is on when it is set.

properties.name: server.ssl.certificate-private-key
properties.description: The private key (a PEM file); required with `certificate`.

properties.name: server.ssl.client-auth
properties.description: Asks clients for a certificate; with `need`, a request without one is answered with 403.

properties.name: server.ssl.enabled
properties.description: `false` ignores the other `server.ssl.*` keys.

properties.name: server.ssl.key-password
properties.description: The password of an encrypted private key.

properties.name: server.ssl.trust-certificate
properties.description: The certificates of trusted clients (a PEM file), for `client-auth`.

properties.name: server.websocket.max-binary-message-size
properties.description: The same for binary messages. `-1` for no limit.

properties.name: server.websocket.max-text-message-size
properties.description: The largest text message a WebSocket session reads, in UTF-8 bytes (Tomcat counts characters); a larger one closes the session with 1009. `-1` for no limit.

properties.name: server.websocket.send-buffer-size-limit
properties.description: How much a WebSocket session may keep waiting to be sent to a client that reads slowly or not at all (pongs included); past it the connection is dropped and the session's close status is 4500 (`sessionNotReliable`). `-1` for no limit.

properties.name: server.websocket.send-time-limit
properties.description: How long what a session sent may take to leave; past it the connection is dropped the same way. `-1` for no limit.

properties.name: spring.main.web-application-type
properties.description: `none`: the beans (and `MockMvc`) exist, but no server starts. Any other value starts the server.

properties.name: spring.mvc.async.request-timeout
properties.description: The timeout of an `SseEmitter` created without one; when it passes, the emitter completes after running its `onTimeout` callbacks. Default: no limit.

properties.name: spring.mvc.log-request-details
properties.description: Shows the parameters and headers of requests in the logs (credentials stay `masked`). Off by default, as they may hold secrets.

properties.name: spring.mvc.sse.heartbeat-interval
properties.description: Sends a comment line in every open event stream at this interval, so proxies keep idle streams open. Default: none.

properties.name: spring.mvc.static-path-pattern
properties.description: The path pattern the static resources of `spring.web.resources.static-locations` are served under: `/**` serves `static/app.css` as `/app.css`, `/assets/**` as `/assets/app.css`. The welcome page (`index.html` at `/`) is served only with `/**`, as in Spring Boot.

properties.name: spring.test.web-environment
properties.description: Set by `springBootTest(webEnvironment:)` (`mock` by default) and by `ApplicationContextRunner` (`mock`): `mock` has no server (`MockMvc` calls the dispatcher in memory), `random-port` a real server on a free port, `defined-port` one on `server.port`, `none` no server. Default: not set: a server starts. Another value starts no server either.

properties.name: spring.web.debug.qps.enabled
properties.description: Whether the application counts its requests: with `true` the build has the filter that counts them and `RequestRates`, which logs the requests per second and answers the actuator's `qps` endpoint; without it, none of that code. Read by the generator.

properties.name: spring.web.debug.qps.log-interval
properties.description: The length of a window: how often the rate is worked out and logged.

properties.name: spring.web.multipart.enabled
properties.description: `false`: `multipart/*` requests are not parsed, and `@RequestPart` parameters answer 400.

properties.name: spring.web.multipart.file-size-threshold
properties.description: Files above this size are written to a temporary file; smaller ones stay in memory.

properties.name: spring.web.multipart.location
properties.description: Where the private directory (`0700`) of the uploads' temporary files is made; the files have random names and are deleted when the request ends or fails. Default: the system's temporary directory.

properties.name: spring.web.multipart.max-file-size
properties.description: The largest file (or other part) of an upload; above it the answer is 413 (`MaxUploadSizeExceededException`). `-1` for no limit.

properties.name: spring.web.multipart.max-part-count
properties.description: The most parts (files and fields) of a multipart request; above it the answer is 413. `-1` for no limit. Spring Boot sets the same limit with `server.tomcat.max-part-count`.

properties.name: spring.web.multipart.max-request-size
properties.description: The largest multipart request as a whole; above it the answer is 413. `-1` for no limit.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.add-mappings
properties.description: `false` turns off the default mapping of `static-locations` under `spring.mvc.static-path-pattern` and the welcome page; mappings a `WebMvcConfigurer` adds stay.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.cachecontrol.cache-private
properties.description: `private`: only the user's own cache may store the answer.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.cachecontrol.cache-public
properties.description: `public`: shared caches may store the answer too.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.cachecontrol.max-age
properties.description: `max-age`: how long the answer may be reused without asking the server. A number without a unit is seconds.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.cachecontrol.must-revalidate
properties.description: `must-revalidate`: once stale, not used without asking the server.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.cachecontrol.no-cache
properties.description: `no-cache`: reused only after the server confirmed it.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.cachecontrol.no-store
properties.description: `no-store`: never stored. Wins over `no-cache` and `max-age`.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.cachecontrol.no-transform
properties.description: `no-transform`: proxies must not change the content.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.cachecontrol.proxy-revalidate
properties.description: `proxy-revalidate`: `must-revalidate` for shared caches only.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.cachecontrol.s-max-age
properties.description: `s-maxage`: how long shared caches may keep the answer. A number without a unit is seconds.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.cachecontrol.stale-if-error
properties.description: `stale-if-error`: how long a stale answer may be used when the server fails. A number without a unit is seconds.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.cachecontrol.stale-while-revalidate
properties.description: `stale-while-revalidate`: how long a stale answer may be used while a fresh one is fetched. A number without a unit is seconds.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.period
properties.description: How long browsers may keep a static resource (`Cache-Control: max-age=` and the seconds); `0` sends `no-store`. A number without a unit is seconds. Default: no `Cache-Control`. The `cachecontrol.*` keys win over it.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.cache.use-last-modified
properties.description: Whether the files' modification time is sent as `Last-Modified` and checked against `If-Modified-Since` (`304`).

properties.name: spring.web.resources.chain.compressed
properties.description: Serves a precompressed file next to the one asked for (`app.js.br`, `app.js.gz`) to a client whose `Accept-Encoding` takes it (Brotli first), with `Content-Encoding` and `Vary: Accept-Encoding`.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.directory-index
properties.description: A path with no file, whose folder holds an `index.html`, gets that `index.html`: `/guide` and `/guide/` are answered with `guide/index.html`, as static hosts (Cloudflare Pages, Netlify) answer. The pages the build writes for search engines (`spring.flutter.web.seo.*`) are such files. Asked before [spaFallback]; the file is found as any other (inside the location, the same checks). Not in Spring Boot, whose welcome page covers `/` only: this starter's own key.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.spa-fallback
properties.description: For a single-page app (a `flutter build web` output, a JavaScript router): a browser's `GET` or `HEAD` of a path that is no file and no handler, whose last segment has no extension and that asks for `text/html` by name, gets the `index.html` of `static-locations` instead of a 404, so deep links work. Not in Spring Boot: this starter's own key.

properties.name: spring.web.resources.static-locations
properties.description: Where the static resources are read from, in order (the first location with the file wins): `resources:` folders of `lib/resources/` (embedded by the generator) and `file:` directories read at run time (`file:web/`, `file:/srv/shop/build/web/`). Spring Boot's defaults with `classpath:` written `resources:`; `META-INF/resources/` and `resources/` are left out, as Dart has no jars.

values.description: The headers are ignored, the default: the request is what reached the server.
The headers of trusted proxies are applied (Spring Boot: the container's own support, Tomcat's `RemoteIpValve`).
Only the application, through the `IsolateScaler` bean.
Stop accepting connections and let running requests finish, for up to `spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase` (30 seconds by default); then close what is left. The default.
Close every connection right away, cutting running requests.
No client certificate is asked for. The default.
A client certificate is asked for; a client without one is served anyway.
A client certificate is required; a request without one gets a 403.
